explanations: terra: Belief in the unseen, prayer, and spending from provision are joined, placing worship and giving under an orientation deeper than human sight.
terra: Some people say publicly that they believe while the verse denies that inward reality, a direct verbal version of the gap between shown form and actual identity.
terra: Their attempt to deceive Allah and believers deceives only themselves, showing that managing human perception cannot manage the true observer.
terra: When challenged over corruption they present themselves as reformers, another attractive public description detached from the action beneath it.
terra: Allah identifies those self-described reformers as corrupters who do not perceive, supplying the deeper judgment their own mirror cannot give.
terra: The hypocrites say they believe when they meet believers and reverse themselves when alone with their devils, a precise case of conduct that exists only before the desired audience.
terra: The rebuke to people who command righteousness of others while forgetting themselves exposes a public religious voice whose own action has no matching depth.
terra: A group professes belief when meeting believers but challenges one another when alone, repeating the section's scene of behavior calibrated to who is looking.
terra: The question reminds them that Allah knows what they conceal and disclose, placing both performances before the viewer they omitted from their calculation.
luna: The covenant joins kindness to orphans and the needy, good speech, and prayer; its next clause says most turned away, gathering the section's care and worship concerns.
terra: Prayer and almsgiving are followed by the assurance that whatever good is sent ahead will be found with Allah, who sees what people do; value rests with the true viewer.

luna: The verse denies that facing east or west alone is righteousness and instead names care for orphans and the poor alongside prayer, reversing outward form without substance. | terra: Righteousness is not exhausted by turning faces in a ritual direction but includes belief, giving to orphans and the needy, and prayer, a direct boundary between religious surface and substance.

luna: The verse describes a person's speech as pleasing to the listener, while its context calls him a fierce opponent; it directs attention from an attractive public surface to character. | terra: A man's speech about worldly life pleases the listener and he invokes Allah concerning his heart, yet Allah identifies him as the fiercest adversary; polished presentation hides his reality.

luna: The continuation shows what that speaker does after turning away: he strives to spread corruption and destroy crops and offspring, supplying conduct beneath the pleasing speech in 2:204. | terra: When that pleasing speaker turns away, his movement through the land exposes corruption and destruction; deed supplies the visible finger pointing to what the man is.
luna: After the speaker's destructive conduct in 2:205, this ayah says that when told to fear Allah, pride drives him into sin, exposing the stance beneath his pleasing words.
terra: Worldly life is beautified for disbelievers who mock believers, but the reverent will be above them at resurrection; present spectatorship and final worth diverge.
luna: Asked about orphans, the reply makes their reformation best and says Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer, linking outward treatment to hidden intent.

luna: This verse describes spending without following it with reminders or harm, a concrete standard for giving that serves the recipient rather than the giver's display. | terra: Those who spend and do not follow the gift with reminders or injury preserve the recipient's good, opposing charity used to construct the giver's public image.

luna: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, so a visible gift cannot excuse harmful treatment of its recipient. | terra: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by hurt, placing the needy person's treatment above the visible fact of giving just before 2:264 names ostentation.

luna: The source's form رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ (“to be seen by people”) occurs here; charity for display is likened to dust on smooth stone washed bare, exposing an outward act without enduring substance. | terra: The spender acts رِئَاءَ ٱلنَّاسِ, and the dust washed from a smooth rock makes the section's mirror-like surface with no depth concrete: the displayed charity leaves nothing to retain.
terra: Spending to seek Allah's pleasure and to make the self firm is the inwardly rooted counterpart to the rain-stripped ostentatious rock of 2:264.
terra: Whatever people spend or vow is known by Allah, assigning the evaluation of giving to a witness beyond the giver's managed audience.

luna: The verse says public charity is good but concealed charity given to the poor is better; it clarifies that the issue is motive and audience, not mere visibility. | terra: The verse approves disclosed charity yet calls concealed giving to the poor better, setting a boundary: visibility itself does not make a deed ostentation, and hidden good has a real recipient.

luna: The verse says spending is for the givers themselves and that they spend seeking only Allah's face, repeating the section's contrast between divine aim and human notice. | terra: Spending is directed to seeking Allah's face and every good expenditure returns to the giver, opposing the act aimed at people's eyes.

luna: The needy do not ask persistently, so an ignorant observer thinks them self-sufficient; the verse urges giving and says Allah knows it, exposing need that a human glance misses. | terra: The unknowing observer mistakes restrained poor people for self-sufficient, while an attentive one recognizes them by their marks; it is a concrete lesson in seeing need beneath appearance.

luna: People who spend secretly and publicly both receive reward from their Lord; this marks the boundary between public giving and giving for show. | terra: Those who spend by night and day, secretly and openly, receive their reward; the public or hidden setting does not determine sincerity by itself.
terra: Whether what is in breasts is concealed or disclosed, Allah knows it, directly placing inner purpose beyond the performer's control of appearances.
terra: They profess belief when meeting believers but bite their fingertips when alone, a second concrete instance of conduct changing with the available audience.
terra: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, locating the section's surface-depth split between a publicly available form and a hidden reality.

luna: It warns those who withhold Allah's bounty not to think it good, and says it will be a burden on the Day of Resurrection, extending the section's hidden withholding into judgment. | terra: Those who withhold Allah's bounty think the act good for them, but it will become a visible collar, turning concealed stinginess into disclosed judgment.

luna: The verse condemns people who want praise for what they have not done, a specific gap between public acclaim and actual deed like the section's display. | terra: Those who love to be praised for what they did not do depend on a public image detached from reality, the same gap between the viewers' impression and the person's actual deed.
terra: The Prophet is told not to be deceived by the disbelievers' movement through the lands, redirecting judgment away from their publicly visible success.
terra: That visible success is only brief enjoyment before a wretched destination, supplying the concealed depth beneath the movement of 3:196.
luna: One command joins worship of Allah with kindness to orphans and the needy, then condemns the arrogant boaster مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا; it gathers the section's ethical and display concerns.

luna: Condemning stinginess and concealing Allah's bounty reverses the section's small, hidden withholding of help. | terra: The same passage that next names ostentatious spending first exposes those who are stingy, urge others to stinginess, and conceal Allah's bounty, closely pairing hidden withholding with public display.

luna: رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ describes spending for a human audience, the same source-root branch as people-facing display; this ayah's specific act is spending wealth. | terra: Spending wealth رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ is the same audience-facing act as 107:6, now placed in giving rather than prayer.
luna: After the display-spending verse, this asks what would prevent belief and spending from Allah's provision, then says Allah knows them; it shifts the audience from people to God.
terra: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم asks the listener to look at people who present themselves as pure, then transfers the authority to purify to Allah.
terra: They say obedience in the Prophet's presence, then a group plots at night to the contrary while Allah records it, an exact audience-dependent reversal between shown and hidden conduct.

luna: The verse says they hide themselves from people but cannot hide from Allah, then describes their night plotting; it names the unseen divine audience behind the section's public display. | terra: They hide from people but cannot hide from Allah, who is with them during their secret plotting; this exactly reverses the show-off's calculation of when an act has an audience.
luna: After the concealment from people but not Allah in 4:108, this ayah contrasts arguing for someone in worldly life with who will argue for him before Allah on the Resurrection.

luna: يُرَاءُونَ النَّاسَ places people as the audience for prayer; the verse calls that prayer lazy, matching the section's visible worship whose reality is governed by who watches. | terra: The exact verb يُرَاءُونَ describes hypocrites rising lazily for prayer in order to be seen by people, the section's central scene of a prayer sustained by its human audience.
luna: Sincerity to Allah after repentance is the explicit reversal of a public religious act whose motive is human sight.
terra: Whether good is disclosed or concealed, it remains good; this sets the section's needed boundary between being visible and being performed for visibility.
terra: Two offerings are outwardly comparable, but acceptance belongs only to the reverent; the result depends on a reality beneath the performed rite.
terra: Some say they believe with their mouths although their hearts do not believe; the Messenger is told not to grieve over this explicit surface-depth split.

luna: Do not drive away those who call on their Lord seeking His face: this directly reverses rejection of the vulnerable and redirects attention to devotion. | terra: The Prophet must not drive away socially slighted worshippers who call on their Lord seeking His face; their unseen aim outweighs an audience's status judgment.
terra: People ask contemptuously whether these are the ones Allah favored among them; Allah's knowledge of the grateful corrects their status-bound gaze at the worshippers of 6:52.
luna: The verse reverses visual agency: human eyes do not encompass Allah, while He encompasses eyes; its context concerns divine incomparability, sharpening who sees without claiming people see God.
terra: Insights have come from the Lord, and whoever truly perceives does so for himself; the verse supports the section's movement from eyesight to inward perception.

luna: The speaker is told to say that his prayer, rites, life, and death are for Allah; prayer's stated audience is therefore the opposite of the people sought by show-offs. | terra: The declaration that prayer, sacrifice, life, and death belong to Allah gives prayer the opposite intended recipient from the human gaze sought in showing off.

terra: Clothing provides visible covering and adornment, while the garment of reverence is declared better; the verse directly distinguishes a person's dress from the deeper quality the section asks one to see.
luna: The command to take adornment at every place of prayer sets a boundary: visible clothing can accompany worship, while the section's concern is the audience and motive behind display.
terra: The true believers establish prayer and spend from provision after their hearts respond to Allah's mention, explicitly joining inward state, worship, and giving.

luna: رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ names display in this verse's departure scene, paired with turning from Allah's way; it shows the same root's public performance in another act. | terra: Those who leave home boastfully and رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ stage themselves before people, while the verse closes by placing their deeds within Allah's encompassing sight.

luna: The verse links coming to prayer lazily with spending only reluctantly, a specific pairing of performed worship and withheld provision like the section's prayer and ma'un. | terra: The hypocrites come to prayer only lazily and spend only unwillingly, so two visible devotions disclose an inward refusal rather than cover it.
terra: The Prophet is told not to be impressed by wealth and children, explicitly refusing visible abundance as evidence of a person's favored reality.
terra: They swear publicly that they belong with the believers although the verse denies it, making an oath the surface of a frightened contrary identity.
terra: Their readiness to flee into any refuge reveals the fear beneath the belonging they displayed in 9:56.
terra: They swear to people in order to please them, while Allah and His Messenger are more entitled to be pleased; the verse identifies a misdirected audience and corrects it.
terra: Hypocrites enjoin wrong, forbid right, and close their hands, joining a communal religious identity to the withholding action that reveals it as hollow.
terra: Believing allies enjoin right, establish prayer, and give alms, providing the integrated social action absent from the showy worshipper's public image.
terra: They covenant that if Allah gives bounty they will give charity and be righteous, establishing the publicly stated image against which their later withholding is read.
terra: When bounty arrives they become stingy and turn away, so action uncovers the person beneath the earlier promise.
terra: Hypocrisy in their hearts results from breaking the promise and lying, explicitly locating the inward reality produced by the outward sequence.
terra: The closing question asks whether they know Allah knows their secret and private counsel, naming the true viewer of what their public promise concealed.
terra: Some hypocrites are unknown even to the Prophet while Allah knows them, a needed boundary on the human gaze summoned by the section.

terra: The command to act says Allah, His Messenger, and the believers will see the deeds, then invokes the Knower of unseen and seen; it names both public witnesses and the gaze that reaches beyond them.

luna: The mosque-builders swear they intended only good, while Allah declares them liars; a public religious setting masks a contrary purpose, close to prayer staged for observers. | terra: A mosque is built for harm and division while its builders swear that they intended only good; a conspicuously religious form functions as a false surface over its purpose.

luna: After the mosque built for harm, disbelief, and division, this ayah forbids standing there and favors the mosque founded on piety, where people seek purification. | terra: The Prophet is forbidden to stand in the harmful mosque and directed to one founded on reverence, distinguishing two outwardly similar prayer settings by their foundations.

luna: It contrasts a building founded on piety and Allah's approval with one on a crumbling bank, making the true foundation of an outward religious structure visible. | terra: The two mosques are distinguished by foundations: reverence and divine pleasure versus the crumbling edge of a precipice, giving architectural depth to the contrast between identical religious surfaces.
terra: The false building remains a source of doubt within its builders' hearts, explicitly joining the displayed structure to the concealed interior named in 9:107.
terra: No deed is begun without Allah witnessing it, and not even an atom's weight is hidden from Him; the verse unites the true spectator with the section's smallest unnoticed act.
terra: Noah's chiefs say they see only low-status followers and judge them بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ, at first glance, embodying the shallow gaze the section rejects.
terra: Noah refuses to drive away the lowly believers because they will meet their Lord and tells the chiefs he sees them acting ignorantly, countering their first-glance judgment in 11:27.
terra: Noah refuses to say that those whom the chiefs' eyes despise will receive no good from Allah, explicitly denying that visible social appearance discloses divine worth.
terra: Joseph's brothers present his shirt with false blood, but Jacob rejects the staged evidence and diagnoses what their selves enticed them to do, a concrete false image read past its surface.

luna: This passage joins prayer, spending secretly and openly, and seeking the face of their Lord, directly contrasting the section's people-facing worship and withheld help. | terra: Seeking the Lord's face, establishing prayer, and spending secretly and openly appear together, providing a compact inverse of public prayer joined to hidden withholding.
terra: Believing servants are told to establish prayer and spend secretly and openly, a boundary against treating public visibility as proof of insincerity while joining prayer to giving.
terra: The Prophet is told not to extend his eyes toward what worldly groups have been given and instead to lower his wing to believers, reversing the spectators' attraction to outward display.
terra: A provisioned person spends secretly and openly in the parable, reinforcing that visibility is a circumstance of giving rather than proof that it is done to be seen.
luna: Hearing, sight, and heart are each said to be questioned, giving the section's named eye-sight and inward insight a concrete accountability before God.
terra: The ban on walking exultantly rejects the body used as a public display of importance and recalls that such posture cannot give the person the greatness it advertises.
luna: The verse says that possession of the Lord's mercy-treasures would make people withhold for fear of spending, a specific parallel to refusing even small aid.

luna: The command not to let one's eyes pass beyond those seeking the Lord's face, for worldly adornment, reverses the section's gaze toward social display. | terra: The Prophet is told not to let his eyes pass beyond sincere worshippers seeking Allah's face toward worldly adornment, explicitly redirecting sight from surface display to inward aim.
terra: Wealth and children are the adornment of worldly life, while enduring righteous deeds are better with the Lord, distinguishing displayed assets from lasting moral substance.
terra: The question whether to identify the greatest losers by deeds resembles the section's attention-call to inspect a person's true condition through action.
terra: Their effort is lost while they think they are doing well, a self-reflection that looks good to its maker while lacking the reality he attributes to it.
terra: The one hoping to meet the Lord must do righteous work and associate no one in worship, a direct boundary against making human spectators partners in a devotional act.
terra: أَفَرَءَيْتَ summons attention to a disbeliever who confidently advertises future wealth and children, exposing a person through the claim he presents.
terra: The reply asks whether he has looked into the unseen or received a covenant, challenging the depth and warrant of the image projected in 19:77.
terra: The Prophet is told not to extend his eyes toward the flower of worldly provision given to others; commanded sight is withdrawn from display and redirected to the Lord's provision.
terra: Even a mustard-seed weight is brought into the just scales, so an apparently negligible hidden refusal cannot remain outside judgment.
terra: Humble hearts, patience, prayer, and spending are listed together, providing an integrated piety opposite to an impressive prayer surface over a closed hand.
terra: Sacrificial meat and blood do not reach Allah, but reverence does, drawing a precise boundary between a ritual's visible material and what gives it value.

luna: It says eyes are not blind, but hearts within chests are blind تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ, naming the difference between eyesight and inward insight in the source's root gloss. | terra: The verse says blindness belongs not to the eyes but to the hearts within breasts, matching the section's distinction between optical seeing and insight into what a person is.
terra: The successful believers are inwardly humble in prayer, supplying the opposite interior to prayer performed for watching people.
terra: Their active concern with purification or almsgiving joins prayer to giving rather than to withholding.

terra: Trade does not distract these people from remembrance, prayer, and almsgiving because they fear a Day on which hearts and eyes overturn; their worship is governed by the final gaze rather than the market's audience.

luna: The thirsty person mistakes a mirage for water but finds nothing on reaching it; this separate visual image parallels the section's mirror that shows an image without depth. | terra: The mirage looks like water to the thirsty but yields nothing when reached, an indirect yet concrete Quranic analogue for the section's image-bearing surface with no depth behind it.

luna: أَرَأَيْتَ asks the listener to consider one who takes desire as a god, then describes sight and heart as covered; it echoes the section's call to see a person's ruling inner orientation. | terra: أَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ directs sight beyond a person's exterior to the desire that actually rules him.
terra: The servants of the Merciful walk humbly and answer ignorance peacefully, providing an outward bearing whose visible form expresses rather than masks inward allegiance.
terra: Noah's people reject belief because low-status people follow him, a repeated scene in which observers mistake social appearance for spiritual identity.
terra: Noah asks what knowledge he has of the followers' deeds, marking the limit of a human observer's access to their true account.
terra: He assigns their accounting to his Lord, transferring final knowledge from the disdainful spectators to the true judge.
terra: He refuses to drive believers away, acting on the deeper appraisal rather than the crowd's surface valuation.
terra: Trust in the Mighty, Merciful One introduces 26:218-219, so dependence is placed on the true viewer rather than on the response of human spectators.

luna: Allah is named as the one who sees the Prophet when he stands; the verse places standing worship within the true audience's sight. | terra: ٱلَّذِى يَرَىٰكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ identifies the One who sees the Prophet when he rises, replacing the human spectators sought by ostentatious prayer with prayer's true witness.

luna: It extends that sight to تَقَلُّبَكَ فِي السَّاجِدِينَ, so the Prophet's movement among those prostrating is seen by Allah. | terra: Allah also sees the Prophet's movement among those prostrating, extending the true gaze through the communal prayer scene.
terra: Worldly provision and adornment are set against what is with Allah as better and more lasting, another boundary between an attractive visible image and actual value.
terra: Qarun's heavy treasures and exultation begin the public-image scene before his adorned appearance, and the warning not to exult already challenges his posture.
terra: He is told to seek the Hereafter, do good, and avoid corruption with what Allah gave him, supplying the unrealized inward use against which his later display is judged.
terra: Qarun claims his wealth came from knowledge he possessed, a flattering self-image that prepares his public appearance in adornment and ignores Allah's deeper knowledge of prior destroyers.
terra: Qarun comes out before his people in his adornment and awakens the desire of worldly spectators, a full scene of a person presenting a glittering image for others to see.
terra: People given knowledge answer Qarun's dazzled spectators that Allah's reward is better, placing a discerning gaze beside the gaze captured by adornment.
terra: The earth swallowing Qarun and his adornment reveals how little substance or protection stood behind the public image staged in 28:79.
terra: The former spectators revise their judgment after Qarun's fall and recognize Allah's apportionment, showing a surface-bound gaze corrected by what the display concealed.

luna: Prayer is said to restrain indecency and wrongdoing; set beside 107's praying people who neglect the orphan and poor, it makes ethical effect a test of the visible act. | terra: Prayer is said to restrain indecency and wrongdoing, giving genuine prayer a moral effect beyond the visible performance criticized in the section.
terra: People know only the outward aspect of worldly life while remaining heedless of the Hereafter, a direct statement of the surface-bound gaze opposed by the section.
luna: Giving relatives, the needy, and travelers their due is joined to seeking Allah's face, pairing care for the vulnerable with the section's question of audience.
terra: A gift meant to increase within people's wealth does not increase with Allah, whereas alms seeking Allah's face does; the verse separates human-facing appearance from divine value.
terra: Establishing prayer, giving alms, and certainty in the Hereafter appear together, reversing the denial, showy prayer, and withholding linked in surah 107.
terra: A mustard-seed weight hidden in a rock, heaven, or earth is brought forth by Allah; the verse makes the section's unnoticed small act fully visible to its true knower.
terra: Luqman joins prayer to commanding right and patient action immediately after the hidden mustard-seed image, showing worship operating when no human eye supplies its value.

luna: Do not turn your cheek contemptuously toward people or walk exultantly: this addresses the public face and bearing that the source's secondary dictionary sense calls displayed demeanor. | terra: The ban on turning one's cheek from people and walking boastfully addresses the body as a public pose, the same outward bearing named in the section's dictionary image.
terra: Moderation in walking and lowering the voice correct the boastful public posture forbidden in 31:18 and gives bodily presentation a truthful measure.
terra: Their sides leave their beds to call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend from His provision; private prayer and giving are united in one ayah.
terra: No soul knows the hidden joy reserved for those deeds, so the unseen act receives an unseen reward beyond any spectators' response.
terra: Fearing people's reaction while Allah has greater right to be feared is a specific boundary between action governed by human eyes and action governed by the true observer.
terra: Not even an atom's weight in heaven or earth is hidden from the Knower of the unseen, so small concealed conduct remains within the true field of vision.
terra: The one whose evil deed is beautified to him فَرَءَاهُ حَسَنًا mistakes a reflected image of goodness for the deed's truth, a close self-directed form of the section's shallow gaze.

luna: The verse joins reciting Allah's book, establishing prayer, and spending secretly and publicly while hoping for a trade that will not perish, the opposite of empty display. | terra: Recitation, prayer, and spending secretly and openly form one faithful practice, contrasting with the split between conspicuous prayer and concealed refusal.
terra: When told to spend from Allah's provision, the disbelievers answer that Allah could feed the needy Himself; their spoken refusal makes denial visible through failure to feed.
terra: The command to worship Allah with religion made sincere for Him gives devotion the exclusive orientation denied by ostentation.
terra: The speaker is commanded to worship Allah sincerely, again locating worship's intended recipient beyond human eyes.
terra: The declaration of worship sincerely for Allah alone makes the reversal of audience explicit.

luna: خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ وَمَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ joins treacherous eyes to what chests conceal, naming the gap between outward display and hidden motive under divine knowledge. | terra: Allah knows the stealthy glance of the eyes and what breasts conceal, explicitly carrying sight past the visible eye into hidden intention.

terra: Those who answer their Lord establish prayer, conduct affairs by consultation, and spend from provision; responsive worship and social giving form one life rather than a displayed ritual shell.

luna: This parallel أَفَرَأَيْتَ passage again names one who takes desire as a god and says hearing, heart, and sight are sealed, making inward perception the issue. | terra: أَفَرَءَيْتَ again exposes desire as a person's real god, then names the sealed heart and veiled sight; it joins commanded scrutiny to failed inward perception.
terra: Disbelievers dismiss revelation because socially disfavored people reached it before them, a specific status-bound gaze that treats audience rank as a measure of truth.
terra: The verse contrasts one on clear proof with people whose evil deeds are beautified to them and who follow desire, linking false self-sight to the reality it conceals.
terra: Allah could show the hypocrites so that the Prophet would know them by their marks, and their tone already discloses them; the verse models the section's gaze through appearance into identity.
terra: If people were pressed for their wealth they would become stingy and Allah would expose their resentments, directly making withholding a disclosure of the heart.
terra: The hearers are called to spend, but some withhold; the verse says stinginess harms the self while Allah remains rich, correcting the withholder's self-interested calculation.
terra: The laggards say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, another specific outward performance exposed by the speaker who knows its interior.
luna: The believers are described as bowing and prostrating while seeking Allah's bounty and pleasure, with a mark of prostration on their faces: outward appearance here accompanies sincere devotion.
terra: The ban on ridicule warns that those socially belittled may be better than their mockers, setting an explicit limit on judgments made from public appearance.
terra: Tribal and social differences make people recognizable, but honor before Allah is measured by reverence known to Him, separating visible identity from actual worth.
luna: At judgment the cover is removed and sight becomes sharp, a specific boundary to the section's call to see a person's reality before the veil is lifted too late.

luna: The righteous sleep little at night, a devotional act done beyond the public audience that the section's show-offs seek. | terra: The righteous sleep little at night, placing worship in a setting largely unavailable to human spectators.

luna: At dawn they ask forgiveness, continuing the private devotion that frames their material care in the next ayah. | terra: They seek forgiveness before dawn, continuing the private devotion that precedes their provision for the needy.

luna: A known right in wealth for the asker and deprived reverses the refusal of even small assistance. | terra: Their wealth contains a right for the asker and deprived, joining unseen worship to material care in the direct reverse of surah 107's split.
terra: The command not to declare yourselves pure because Allah best knows the reverent blocks the flattering image a person presents of himself and assigns the deeper judgment to Allah.

luna: أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ uses the attention-directing question for one who turns away, then its own context exposes his giving and withholding. | terra: أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ uses the same attention-demand to expose a person by his turning away rather than by his presented appearance.

luna: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰ says he gives little then stops; that concrete withholding echoes the section's small aid and completes the same see-and-judge scene. | terra: The man gives a little and then withholds, an unusually close parallel to the small aid withheld at 107:7 after an outwardly visible religious posture.
terra: The question whether he possesses knowledge of the unseen فَهُوَ يَرَىٰ turns seeing into a challenge to his shallow self-assurance and completes the portrait begun at 53:33.
terra: Worldly life is described as adornment and mutual boasting before its growth withers, making public display a surface whose apparent value cannot endure.

luna: This ayah condemns people who are stingy and urge others to be stingy, turning the section's absent encouragement to feed the poor into active encouragement of withholding. | terra: The verse repeats the portrait of people who are stingy and command others to stinginess, extending the section's concern from a withheld object to a hidden social influence.
terra: No private conversation escapes Allah's presence and eventual disclosure, extending the true audience into precisely the setting where people suppose no one sees.
terra: People return to forbidden private counsels and speak of sin while supposing secrecy, giving the divine presence named in 58:7 a concrete hidden action to observe.
terra: The question why believers say what they do not do forces the hearer to inspect the distance between presented speech and action.
terra: Allah's hatred of saying what is not done supplies the divine valuation concealed by the speaker's public words.

luna: The hypocrites publicly testify to the Messenger, while the same ayah declares them liars; this makes the displayed statement diverge from inward truth. | terra: The hypocrites publicly testify to the Messenger while Allah testifies that they lie; the verse sets a polished declaration before the observer who knows its absent depth.

luna: They use oaths as a shield and turn people from Allah's way, extending the prior verse's false public testimony into action. | terra: The hypocrites use their oaths as a shield, turning visible pious speech into an instrument that hides and protects the contrary deed.
luna: The passage says they believed then disbelieved and their hearts were sealed, specifying the concealed state behind the outward presentation.

luna: When seen, their bodies impress, yet the verse compares them to propped-up timber; this visual contrast between pleasing exterior and inert appearance meets the section's mirror and demeanor image. | terra: When seen, the hypocrites' bodies impress, yet they are likened to propped timbers; the verse directly opposes attractive visible form to the lack of depth behind it.
terra: The hypocrites privately command others not to spend on those with the Messenger so that they disperse, a hidden exhortation to withhold that exposes the reality behind their public testimony.
terra: Allah knows what people conceal and disclose and what breasts contain, a repeated formulation of the depth unavailable to the human audience.
terra: Whether speech is concealed or voiced aloud, Allah knows what breasts contain, directly joining presentation and intention under one knowledge.
terra: The Creator's subtle awareness grounds the preceding claim that hidden speech and hearts cannot escape Him.
luna: The gardeners whisper to one another as they approach their field; the next ayah reveals their concealed plan to exclude the poor.
luna: The gardeners explicitly bar a poor person from entering; their deliberate exclusion makes visible the refusal of food and help that the section diagnoses.

luna: The preceding ayah says this same figure did not believe in Allah the Great; it completes the adjacent accusation of not urging food in 69:34. | terra: Failure to believe in Allah the Great supplies the inward condition paired in the next ayah with the unseen failure to urge feeding the poor.

luna: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ repeats the section's specific accusation that the person does not urge feeding the needy. | terra: The condemned person did not urge feeding the poor; this repeated negative act confirms that an omission no crowd notices can reveal the denier.
terra: The passage diagnoses the human being as anxiously grasping before contrasting that disposition with genuine prayer and a known right for the needy.
terra: Distress makes the person panic, part of the inner portrait whose next movement is withholding when good reaches him.

luna: When good reaches a person, he withholds; this names the disposition behind the section's refusal of small assistance. | terra: When good touches him he becomes withholding, the exact disposition from which the consistent worshippers of 70:22 are excepted.

luna: The next ayah begins the exception, “except those who pray,” whose steadiness and known share for the needy are described in 70:23-25. | terra: The praying are excepted from the human tendency to withhold, beginning a direct reversal of the worshippers in surah 107.

luna: These people are constant in prayer, unlike the section's people whose prayer is inattentive and governed by display. | terra: Their constancy in prayer contrasts with a prayer dependent on whether people are present to see it.
luna: A known share for the asker in one's wealth reverses withholding aid. | terra: A recognized right in their wealth prevents prayer from becoming a public surface over private withholding.

luna: The share extends to the deprived, completing the reversal of neglected need. | terra: That right belongs to the asker and the deprived, completing the inverse relation between genuine prayer and care for those in need.
luna: The passage later says they guard their prayers, completing its picture of sustained worship rather than prayer for an audience.
terra: The question asking what put them in the Fire calls for an account, and the succeeding answers reveal prayer, feeding, and denial as the hidden truth of their lives.

luna: In their own account of punishment they say they were not among those who prayed, a direct counterpart to the section's prayer scene. | terra: The people of the Fire confess that they were not among those who prayed, placing the reality of prayer under final disclosure rather than present appearance.

luna: They also say they did not feed the poor, repeating the section's specific ethical failure. | terra: Their next confession is that they did not feed the poor, joining prayer and care for the needy in the same diagnostic sequence as surah 107.
terra: Joining those engaged in empty talk adds the social company before which their conduct occurred, between neglected care and denial of judgment.

luna: They say they denied the Day of Recompense, linking the social and prayer failures in this passage to 107's opening description of denying الدين. | terra: Their confession that they denied the Day of Judgment supplies the hidden denial that the failures of prayer and feeding reveal.

luna: The human is described as بصيرة against himself even while offering excuses, shifting the decisive witness inward from the audience he presents himself to. | terra: The human being is a witness with insight against himself even while offering excuses, so self-presentation cannot erase the deeper testimony the section asks the hearer to reach.
terra: The person neither affirmed nor prayed, beginning another sequence in which denial, prayer, and publicly legible bodily conduct expose one character.
terra: He instead denied and turned away, closely echoing the denial and turning scrutinized in 96:13 and the denier identified in 107:1.
terra: He then goes to his people swaggering, giving denial an outward posture presented before his social circle.

luna: Feeding the needy, orphan, and captive is the explicit positive reversal of not urging food for the poor. | terra: Feeding the poor, orphan, and captive supplies the enacted care missing from surah 107 and is the deed whose unseen motive is voiced in the next ayah.

luna: The feeders seek Allah's face and neither repayment nor thanks, reversing prayer and action performed for human notice. | terra: The givers feed only for Allah's face and seek neither recompense nor thanks, the explicit opposite of acting so that people will look and respond.
luna: The next ayah says they fear a day from their Lord, completing the motive behind the God-directed feeding described in 76:8-9.

luna: The rebuke عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ opens a scene where attention turns away from a vulnerable seeker toward a prominent man, dramatizing whom the observer chooses to see. | terra: The frown is a visible facial act whose moral meaning Allah calls the addressee to inspect, closely matching the section's way of identifying a person through a small movement.

luna: The next ayah identifies the entrant as blind, making the neglected person's vulnerability explicit. | terra: The occasion is the arrival of a blind man, making physical sight and the failure to perceive a person's worth part of the same scene.

luna: Allah asks whether the blind seeker might attain purity, showing why his inner response matters more than his status. | terra: The question raises the visitor's unseen possibility of purification, directing judgment beyond what his outward status disclosed.

luna: The continuation asks whether he might receive a reminder that benefits him, completing the reason to attend to the seeker. | terra: The visitor might receive a reminder that benefits him, naming an inward effect unavailable to the shallow social appraisal that first dismissed him.

luna: As for the self-sufficient man, the passage changes its description of the person receiving attention, a specific contrast with the seeker who fears and hopes to grow. | terra: Attention turns toward the person who presents himself as self-sufficient, recalling the false self-sight of 96:7 and the section's attractive surface.

luna: The Prophet attends to that self-sufficient man, making the misdirected human gaze explicit in the scene. | terra: The addressee gives the self-sufficient man attentive reception, staging the human gaze as a scarce good directed by visible rank.

luna: The verse says the Prophet is not responsible if the self-sufficient man fails to purify himself, clarifying why that audience should not displace the seeker. | terra: The addressee is not accountable for that man's refusal to purify himself, correcting the social calculation that made him the preferred spectator.

luna: The passage returns to the one who came striving, restoring attention to the vulnerable person previously overlooked. | terra: The sincere seeker comes eagerly, so his movement provides the evidence of character that social appearance had obscured.

luna: The seeker fears Allah, an inward state invisible in status or appearance but decisive in this scene. | terra: The blind seeker's inward fear is the reality beneath his unimportant outward standing.

luna: The final contrast says attention is diverted from that God-fearing seeker, making this an especially close parallel to the section's two audiences. | terra: Turning attention away from the sincere seeker completes a scene in which the commanded gaze must be corrected from prestige to inward receptivity.
terra: Guardians stand over human beings even when no human spectator is present, challenging the premise that an unseen act has no witness.
terra: The guardians are noble recorders, giving the hidden deed a durable account rather than the passing image sought from people.
terra: They know what people do, completing the alternative audience introduced in 82:10.
terra: More indirectly, criminals see the believers and declare them astray; their confident human gaze supplies a concrete instance of spectators judging persons without access to their truth.
terra: The Last Day reverses the spectatorship as believers laugh at the disbelievers, though the link to ostentatious worship is indirect and depends on the neighboring gaze scenes.
terra: The believers are seated looking on, completing the reversal of 83:32; it illuminates the fallibility of the earlier human audience rather than showing off itself.
terra: The Lord is described as being on watch immediately before the human being misreads wealth as honor and his treatment of orphan and poor is exposed.
terra: A person reads abundant provision as proof that his Lord has honored him, judging his own worth by the visible surface of wealth before 89:17 corrects him.
terra: He reads restricted provision as humiliation, another shallow self-judgment overturned by the following exposure of how he treats the vulnerable.

luna: The verse says they do not honor the orphan, a direct social counterpart to 107's figure who pushes the orphan. | terra: The rebuke that they do not honor the orphan identifies moral reality through treatment of the vulnerable, as the pointing gesture of 107:2 identifies the denier.

luna: It adds that they do not encourage feeding the poor, closely matching the section's account of an absent exhortation. | terra: They do not urge one another to feed the poor, the exact kind of absent and easily unseen exhortation that the section says must also be noticed.

luna: After the orphan and poor accusations, this ayah says they devour inheritance greedily, extending the same passage's account of material harm to the vulnerable. | terra: Greedily consuming inheritance continues the concrete actions through which the false self-assessment of 89:15-16 is exposed.

luna: The passage names their intense love of wealth after describing neglect of orphan and poor, supplying a motive for withholding. | terra: Excessive love of wealth names the inward attachment behind the visible failures toward orphan and poor.
terra: The question asking what can make the hearer know the steep path is another attention-command whose answer comes through costly care rather than displayed form.
terra: Freeing a person from bondage begins the answer to 90:12 with an unambiguously beneficial act before the feeding of orphan and poor.

luna: Feeding in a day of hunger reverses the failure to urge food for the needy. | terra: Feeding on a day of hunger supplies active care where the denier's failure to encourage feeding was invisible.
luna: The recipient is an orphan of near kin, reversing the section's mistreatment of an orphan. | terra: The recipient is an orphan of kin, sharpening the reversal of pushing an orphan away.

luna: The passage completes its list with a needy person in misery, the counterpart to withheld aid. | terra: The second recipient is a poor person in misery, completing the reversal of withholding food and small aid.

luna: The contrasting person gives and fears Allah, joining generosity to an inward orientation rather than an audience. | terra: The one who gives and is reverent opens the opposite path from the stingy, self-sufficient person of 92:8.

luna: He confirms al-husna, completing the good person's motive in the passage that turns in 92:8-9 to stinginess and denial. | terra: Affirming the best names the inward conviction expressed through the giver's action.

luna: The next ayah says Allah eases him toward ease, completing the consequence for the giver in contrast with 92:10. | terra: Being eased toward ease discloses the giver's true direction, against the hardship hidden beneath the withholder's self-image.

luna: This ayah describes the stingy person who sees himself as self-sufficient, closely joining the section's 96:7 self-perception to its refusal of aid. | terra: The one who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient joins concealed withholding to the same false self-appraisal depicted in 96:7.

luna: It adds that this person denies al-husna, completing the specific pairing of self-sufficiency, denial, and withholding. | terra: His denial of the best names the inward rejection disclosed through the stinginess of 92:8.

luna: After describing stinginess and denial in 92:8-9, this ayah says the way is eased toward hardship, completing that contrary path. | terra: Being eased toward hardship reveals the actual direction hidden beneath his self-sufficient image.

luna: This person gives wealth to purify himself, a concrete opposite to outward devotion that serves an audience. | terra: The giver offers wealth to purify himself, providing the charitable action whose inward direction 92:19-20 then distinguishes from social exchange and display.

luna: The giver has no favor owed by anyone to repay, the opposite of acting for a human return. | terra: No one's prior favor is being repaid, removing a human audience or social debt as the explanation of the gift.

luna: The act seeks only the face of the Most High Lord, naming the opposite audience from people who are shown a deed. | terra: Seeking only the face of the Most High Lord directs the act toward the opposite gaze from the one sought by ostentation.

luna: The command not to oppress an orphan directly reverses the section's image of a hand pushing one away. | terra: The command not to oppress the orphan directly reverses the hand that pushes the orphan away in 107:2.

luna: The command not to repel the asker reverses refusal of attention and aid to those in need. | terra: The command not to rebuff the petitioner reverses the unnoticed refusal of small help with which the section ends.
terra: This verse identifies the person beneath the prayer confrontation as a human being who transgresses, preparing the deeper diagnosis that outward conduct reveals.
terra: أَن رَّءَاهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ makes false self-sight the cause of transgression: the person holds a flattering mirror to himself and sees independence.

luna: After the self-sufficient man's claim in 96:6-7, this ayah says the return is to the Lord, limiting the imagined independence that the section identifies. | terra: Return is to the Lord, correcting the self-sufficient image of 96:7 and grounding the later reminder that Allah sees.

luna: The exact opening أَرَأَيْتَ redirects attention to the one forbidding prayer; as in the section, the question asks the listener to recognize a person's conduct, not report literal sight. | terra: أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يَنْهَىٰ repeats the section's opening call to look and directs it at a man whose true character appears in what he does around prayer.

luna: The next ayah names the servant praying, completing the scene of prayer being obstructed and supplying the visible act against which 107 sets people-facing worship. | terra: The prohibited object is عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّىٰٓ; this row supplies the praying servant on whom the gaze of 96:9 is fixed.

luna: The repeated “Have you seen?” asks whether the praying servant is upon guidance, placing his inward direction against the one who forbids him. | terra: The repeated interrogative asks whether the praying servant is upon guidance, moving the gaze from the visible prayer scene to the servant's actual moral condition.

luna: The next question asks whether that servant enjoins piety, giving the prayerful figure an ethical action that contrasts with obstruction. | terra: The same interrogative sequence asks whether the servant commands reverence, making an otherwise unseen exhortation part of the evidence, as 107:3 does with the missing exhortation to feed.

luna: The second أَرَأَيْتَ asks the Prophet to consider one who denies and turns away; the formula again summons judgment of character rather than surface looking. | terra: أَرَءَيْتَ again demands an answer about one who denies and turns away, closely joining the gaze-command to the denial named in 107:1.

luna: ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ names the actual seer in this passage, completing the contrast between people's gaze sought by performers and divine sight. | terra: أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ names Allah as the decisive viewer after the human being has been summoned to look.

luna: Sincere worship, prayer, and zakah are the stated opposite of acting religiously for people's eyes. | terra: Sincere worship directed exclusively to Allah is joined to prayer and almsgiving, the integrated opposite of prayer performed for people while aid is withheld.
terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of good يَرَهُ makes even the tiniest deed an eventual object of sight, answering the hidden small kindness at the section's close.
terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of evil يَرَهُ brings an unseen petty refusal under a gaze from which its smallness cannot hide it.
